title: Public dense ZZ generated-resource cutover
objective: Make public dense ZZ matrices canonically own generated FmpzMatrix resources and route all supported structural and algebraic operations through declared resources with Sage-compatible semantics and competitive performance

handoff.summary: Public dense ZZ Matrix values now canonically own generated FmpzMatrix resources. Construction, mutation, inspection, structural arithmetic, multiplication, powers, determinant, rank, HNF/SNF with transformations, exact right kernels, characteristic/minimal polynomials, formatting, serialization, stacking, augmentation, and indexed row/column selection stay resource-to-resource. Packed exact storage is materialized only at explicit list, subdivided formatting, and stable serialization boundaries. Native-disabled execution retains tested correct bulk-ingress fallbacks, and focused tests prohibit hidden packed materialization in resource algorithms.
risks: Generated exact matrix resources remain Node-only declarations with wasm=False; portable opaque-resource lowering is a separate architecture milestone.

Indexed row/column selection is resource-to-resource but currently performs two generated FFI calls per selected row or column. At 250 selected indices from a 500 by 500 matrix it takes about 19--21 ms, versus 2.5--2.7 ms for the former canonical packed path; direct declared resource selectors are required before claiming uniform structural performance.

The aggregate pnpm ffi:lifecycle:fuzz command cannot start in this isolated worktree because the unrelated graph addon is not provisioned. The focused FmpzMatrix lifecycle test passes 300 ownership rounds plus randomized differential checks.
The rebased declaration identity required regenerating the ignored local FLINT host adapter before native validation; generated build artifacts are intentionally not committed.
pnpm parallel:check cannot select this task because the rebased shared worktree contains five other integrated contracts still marked active or review; task-specific validation receipts are current.
next_steps: Integrate onto the generated-resource FFI base and regenerate native host adapters before testing.
Add generated FmpzMatrix select_rows and select_columns operations so indexed selection crosses the resource boundary once instead of twice per selected index.
Apply the same canonical-resource cutover and no-hidden-materialization performance ratchets to remaining exact matrix and polynomial families.
Prove the same opaque-resource declarations through the WASM host lowering before enabling browser resource storage.
